expected.snippet: Because the Court finds that petitioner substantially understated his income tax, the Court will not address whether his underpayment of tax was attributable to negligence.

issues_outside_coverage: State and local general sales tax deduction: notice allowance of $1,466 (claimed $8,350) sustained; total SALT $8,344 under the $10,000 cap
Amount of gambling winnings: reported $30,100 not reduced (petitioner's $12,221 claim rejected for lack of substantiation/credibility)
Conceded Schedule C deductions (other expenses $701, travel $2,360, car and truck $7,274)
Computational Social Security RRB adjustment in the notice (not separately decided)
decisive_judgment_findings: Petitioner's testimony that 2020 gambling winnings were only $12,221 was not credible; no diary, W-2Gs, or admitted documents supported it, and the record's win-loss statements were his spouse's.
Petitioner did not show gambling losses greater than the $16,140 the IRS allowed and on brief did not dispute that amount.
Petitioner kept no receipts to substantiate sales taxes beyond the table amount the IRS allowed (he himself proposed $1,456).
Supervisory tax specialist signed the Civil Penalty Approval Form; petitioner guessed at gambling figures and kept inadequate records, so no reasonable cause or good faith.
